newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan city shocked that murder suspect a schoolboy.
newsitem.headline: Japan city shocked that murder suspect a schoolboy.

text.p: Fear gave way to consternation in the central Japanese city of Kobe on Monday over the weekend arrest and alleged confession of a 14-year-old schoolboy in the murder and beheading of an 11-year-old boy.

The arrest on Saturday of the alleged killer, whose name was not released because he is a minor, came just over a month after the discovery of 11-year-old Jun Hase's mutilated body stunned a nation that prides itself on safe streets.

But if the arrest of a suspect relieved parents who feared that a serial killer might be stalking the streets of Kobe, residents found little relief in the fact the self-confessed murderer had been a neighbour and acquaintance of the victim.
"We are shocked and terribly pained to learn that the suspect turned out to be a junior high school student," said Akiko Hashimoto, principal of the elementary school Jun Hase attended.

The arrest has also caused soul-searching at schools because prosecutors quoted the suspect as saying he killed his 11-year-old acquaintance "because he felt resentment against the school he has been going to".

At Tomogaoka Junior High School, which the suspect attended and where the slain boy's head was found next to the school gate on May 27, sombre students dodged throngs of reporters, and teachers held special counselling sessions.
Japanese media reports said that at around the time of the slaying the young suspect had been suspended from school for an attack on a fellow student.
A letter sent to a local newspaper 10 days after the grisly crime, purporting to be from the killer, blamed Japan's authoritarian education system.
"I am not forgetting revenge for the compulsory education that has produced me as an invisible existence and on the society that has produced this compulsory education," the rambling note said.

Meanwhile, media offered gruesome details of how the suspect lured the victim to a wooded area on May 24 and killed him, then came back a day later to sever and retrieve the head, which he briefly hid at home.
The suspect told police he was "irritated" that day and wanted to "kill someone -- anyone would do", Kyodo news agency quoted police sources as saying.
The suspect enticed Jun Hase to join him to play on a local hill, then strangled the boy about an hour later at a cable television antenna tower at the top of the hill, the report said.

The suspect returned to the scene the next day and beheaded the victim with a knife and a saw, the report said. He left the body at the tower, put the head in a plastic bag and stashed it on a different hill, it said.
He retrieved the head on May 26 and hid it overnight in his home before leaving it by the gate of his school the next morning, it said.
In a related report, Kyodo quoted lawyers for the suspect as protesting that the 14-year-old's identity had been disclosed on the Internet.
